title: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians
body:
IUIC in the ClassRoom · 2026-02-28

Opens [Neh 10](/bible/nehemiah/10) · [2 Pet 3](/bible/2-peter/3) · [Gal 1](/bible/galatians/1) · [Gal 2](/bible/galatians/2) · [Gal 3](/bible/galatians/3) · [Gal 4](/bible/galatians/4) · [1 Pet 1](/bible/1-peter/1)
## Introduction *[[7:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XOMlLvwK8mI&t=424s)]* Navigating through Paul's letters: a walk through Galatians, continuing a series that began with Acts 10, Romans 11, and Romans 3 through 5. Peter vouched for all of Paul's epistles as written by the wisdom given him, hard to be understood, and twisted by the unlearned and unstable. The class works Galatians 1 through 4 verse by verse: the gospel is exclusive to Israel and any other gospel is accursed; the Gentiles Paul writes to are the dispersed Israelites among the nations; the works of the law that no man is justified by are the sacrificial law of Nehemiah 10:33; the curse of the law is death, which Christ took by hanging on a tree; the schoolmaster, the bondage, and the weak and beggarly elements are animal sacrifice, which the Pharisees kept trying to bring the churches back into; and Peter's first letter names the strangers scattered in Galatia a chosen generation and a holy nation. ## In The News - *[[1:38:25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XOMlLvwK8mI&t=5905s)]* **An AI answer on the term Antiochians, read on screen.** — In 175 BC Jason bribed Antiochus IV to turn Jerusalem into a Greek-style polis and enrol its people as citizens of Antioch. Registered Israelites were called Antiochians, a betrayal of their ancestral laws and a shift to the Greek way of life that triggered the Maccabean revolt. Antiochian and Greek are synonymous, so neither Jew nor Greek is written to those Israelites' descendants. ## Scriptures Opened **[Nehemiah 10:33](/bible/nehemiah/10#v33)** *[[7:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XOMlLvwK8mI&t=470s)]* > [33](/bible/nehemiah/10#v33) For the shewbread, and for the continual meat offering, and for the continual burnt offering, of the sabbaths, of the new moons, for the set feasts, and for the holy things, and for the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God. - The showbread, the continual meat offering, the burnt offerings of the Sabbaths, new moons, and set feasts, the holy things, and the sin offerings, to make an atonement for Israel, and all the work of the house of our God. Atonement, reconciliation, and justification are the same thing, covered in Romans 5. That is the works: write this down, because it is the answer to every works of the law in Galatians. - The comment boards on these classes are not chalkboards. Christians who cower on Clubhouse and will not come on stage do not get to teach in the comments. **[2 Peter 3:15-18](/bible/2-peter/3#v15)** *[[11:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XOMlLvwK8mI&t=670s)]* > [15](/bible/2-peter/3#v15) And account that the longsuffering of our Lord is salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you; > > [16](/bible/2-peter/3#v16) As also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction. > > [17](/bible/2-peter/3#v17) Ye therefore, beloved, seeing ye know these things before, beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness. > > [18](/bible/2-peter/3#v18) But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and for ever. Amen. - Our beloved brother Paul, according to the wisdom given unto him, hath written unto you. Wisdom is not a what but a who: Christ. Peter read all his epistles and did not let anything erroneous slide. If Paul wrote error it implicates Peter, James, and John, the last surviving disciple, and makes Christ a negligent Messiah who waited three thousand years to send someone to fix Paul. - In which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, the law and the prophets, unto their own destruction. Wrest is wrestle: they twist Paul into something he did not say, because they do not believe what the Bible really says. - Beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own steadfastness. The error of the wicked says all nations can be saved, Paul grafted the nations in, adultery is permitted, the Sabbath changed, and the laws are done away. Grow in grace and in the knowledge of our Lord. Precepts: - **[Acts 26:22](/bible/acts/26#v22)** > [22](/bible/acts/26#v22) Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come: Paul witnessed none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come. The law and the prophets were his source material. - **[Acts 28:23](/bible/acts/28#v23)** > [23](/bible/acts/28#v23) And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening. He expounded the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus both out of the law of Moses and out of the prophets, from morning till evening. Paul's letters, from the forties to sixties AD, predate the gospels except Mark, who scribed for Peter, and possibly Matthew; John was written around 90 AD, twenty years after Rome's siege of Jerusalem. Paul was not quoting John 3:16. Luke, who travelled with him, wrote Luke and Acts, a second Luke. **[Galatians 1:2-16](/bible/galatians/1#v2)** *[[20:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XOMlLvwK8mI&t=1210s)]* > [2](/bible/galatians/1#v2) And all the brethren which are with me, unto the churches of Galatia: > > [3](/bible/galatians/1#v3) Grace be to you and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ, > > [4](/bible/galatians/1#v4) Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father: > > [5](/bible/galatians/1#v5) To whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen. > > [6](/bible/galatians/1#v6) I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: > > [7](/bible/galatians/1#v7) Which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ. > > [8](/bible/galatians/1#v8) But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed. > > [9](/bible/galatians/1#v9) As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed. > > [10](/bible/galatians/1#v10) For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ. > > [11](/bible/galatians/1#v11) But I certify you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached of me is not after man. > > [12](/bible/galatians/1#v12) For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ. > > [13](/bible/galatians/1#v13) For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews’ religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it: > > [14](/bible/galatians/1#v14) And profited in the Jews’ religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers. > > [15](/bible/galatians/1#v15) But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother’s womb, and called me by his grace, > > [16](/bible/galatians/1#v16) To reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood: - Grace and peace from our Lord Jesus Christ, who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil world. Those possessive words, our sins and deliver us, are not everyone. - I marvel that ye are so soon removed unto another gospel, which is not another, but there be some that trouble you and would pervert the gospel of Christ. Then it was Pharisees and Sadducees infiltrating; today it is Christian pastors and Israelites slowly seeping into the Christianity cult doctrine. Though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel, let him be accursed. - The gospel is the good news for Israelites: a black Messiah who died for the sins of his people alone, and divine reparations and justice after our time in America. Including your enemies in it is another gospel, like delivering the newspaper or your food to the wrong house. The danger of teaching nations to be saved is that you are accursed. Catholic means inclusive; the Bible is exclusive, and God calls us a peculiar people. - The gospel preached of me is not after man; I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ. Paul's advice to stay single was advice, but even that was the spirit of the Lord. He profited in the Jews' religion above many his equals, raised a Pharisee from a prestigious family, zealous of the traditions of his fathers. - It pleased God, who separated me from my mother's womb, to reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen. Paul was called from birth despite the harm he did to the church, and Christ speaks through him; the error of the wicked calls that his opinion. Among the heathen, among the Gentiles: Israel was scattered among the nations, and that is who he writes to the entire time. **[Galatians 2:1-16](/bible/galatians/2#v1)** *[[28:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XOMlLvwK8mI&t=1729s)]* > [1](/bible/galatians/2#v1) Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also. > > [2](/bible/galatians/2#v2) And I went up by revelation, and communicated unto them that gospel which I preach among the Gentiles, but privately to them which were of reputation, lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain. > > [3](/bible/galatians/2#v3) But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised: > > [4](/bible/galatians/2#v4) And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage: > > [5](/bible/galatians/2#v5) To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you. > > [6](/bible/galatians/2#v6) But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no man’s person:) for they who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me: > > [7](/bible/galatians/2#v7) But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter; > > [8](/bible/galatians/2#v8) (For he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles:) > > [9](/bible/galatians/2#v9) And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision. > > [10](/bible/galatians/2#v10) Only they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do. > > [11](/bible/galatians/2#v11) But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. > > [12](/bible/galatians/2#v12) For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. > > [13](/bible/galatians/2#v13) And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation. > > [14](/bible/galatians/2#v14) But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews? > > [15](/bible/galatians/2#v15) We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles, > > [16](/bible/galatians/2#v16) Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified. - Fourteen years after, Paul went up to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus and communicated the gospel he preached among the Gentiles, privately to them of reputation, to those he could trust, lest he had run in vain. Titus, being a Greek, was not compelled to be circumcised; the Greek part is unfolded later. - False brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage. Keep liberty and bondage in mind. To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour: to hell with them, whatever reputation, school, or camp they had. God accepteth no man's person, and they added nothing to me. - They saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter, for he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles. Christ worked in Peter toward the Jews born and raised in the law and circumcised the eighth day, and the same Christ worked in Paul toward the dispersed. James, Cephas, and John gave the right hands of fellowship that we should go unto the heathen and they unto the circumcision, remembering the poor. - When Peter was come to Antioch, in Turkey like Galatia, I withstood him to the face. He ate with the Gentiles, but when certain came from James he withdrew, fearing them of the circumcision, and the other Jews and even Barnabas dissembled with him. If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of the Gentiles, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews? You cannot teach the scattered sinners of the Gentiles who they are and then act like you are not with them; that is a bad example. - Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ. Here is where the other gospel and the error of the wicked come in: all you have to do is believe, you can lie, cheat, steal, and rape in the name of Jesus, as a Dominican in the Bronx once told me. Works of the law, law singular, shout out to Captain Zakar: the law of sacrifice from Nehemiah 10:33. A man no longer receives atonement by sacrificial law, for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified. Christians will run to Galatians 2:16, 3:2, and 3:5; these are their go-tos, and I am giving you the tools. Precepts: - **[John 7:35](/bible/john/7#v35)** > [35](/bible/john/7#v35) Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles? Then said the Jews, whither will he go that we shall not find him? Will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles? The dispersed are Israelites, and the Jews of the circumcision call the dispersed Israelites Gentiles. Now you know who the Gentiles are that Paul writes to. **[Galatians 3:1-9](/bible/galatians/3#v1)** *[[46:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XOMlLvwK8mI&t=2778s)]* > [1](/bible/galatians/3#v1) O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you? > > [2](/bible/galatians/3#v2) This only would I learn of you, Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? > > [3](/bible/galatians/3#v3) Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh? > > [4](/bible/galatians/3#v4) Have ye suffered so many things in vain? if it be yet in vain. > > [5](/bible/galatians/3#v5) He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? > > [6](/bible/galatians/3#v6) Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness. > > [7](/bible/galatians/3#v7) Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham. > > [8](/bible/galatians/3#v8) And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed. > > [9](/bible/galatians/3#v9) So then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham. - Christ's death freed us from having to atone with animals; that is the liberty being spied out, because the temple is gone and the priests are scattered. If you seek to be justified by animals you are condemned by default, since there is no animal for sins worthy of death: selling drugs is witchcraft and sorcery, pimping is whoremongering, worshipping Cesare Borgia is idolatry, and Catholic, Baptist, and Muslim are condemned. Thank Christ for dying for you. And you are not David, Moses, or Solomon; the exception does not change the rule, it proves it. - O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth? Someone was going into each church spreading misinformation: an infiltration, people saying I believe and then teaching contrary to what they were sent to teach. Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? Are ye so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh of animals? Have ye suffered so many things in vain? He that worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law? Verses 2 and 5 are the same sacrifice as 2:16. - Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness. God promised him a son and land and seed as the sand of the sea, Abraham believed, and only afterward offered sacrifices; his faith came first and that was counted for righteousness, not the animal. They which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham. - The scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, the Israelites scattered among the Gentiles, preached before the gospel unto Abraham: in thee shall all nations be blessed. See, brother, all nations. No: Esau already got his blessing, blood and death and slavery, weaponry, war, nukes, and witchcraft; he is dropping his blessings on Iran right now. Your blessing is to work, build up our kingdom, and survive the destruction as servants. They which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham. Precepts: - **[Acts 3:24-26](/bible/acts/3#v24)** > [24](/bible/acts/3#v24) Yea, and all the prophets from Samuel and those that follow after, as many as have spoken, have likewise foretold of these days. > > [25](/bible/acts/3#v25) Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed. > > [26](/bible/acts/3#v26) Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities. Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, and in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed. Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities. The blessing on all kindreds of the earth is Christ dying for the Israelites scattered in every nation, whose blood covers us wherever we are found, since we cannot reach all our people on this earth. - **[Isaiah 45:25](/bible/isaiah/45#v25)** > [25](/bible/isaiah/45#v25) In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory. In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory. Whether called Jews or Gentiles, all the seed of Israel is justified by faith in Christ. Show me one precept where all the seed of Edom, Moab, Ishmael, or Canaan is justified; it is nowhere in the law and prophets. **[Galatians 3:10-14](/bible/galatians/3#v10)** *[[1:00:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XOMlLvwK8mI&t=3619s)]* > [10](/bible/galatians/3#v10) For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them. > > [11](/bible/galatians/3#v11) But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith. > > [12](/bible/galatians/3#v12) And the law is not of faith: but, The man that doeth them shall live in them. > > [13](/bible/galatians/3#v13) Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree: > > [14](/bible/galatians/3#v14) That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith. - For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse, for it is written, cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them. Works of the law in verses 2, 5, and 10 and in 2:16 is sacrifice, Nehemiah 10:33. Under the curse means under the curse of the covenant. - No man is justified by the law in the sight of God, for the just shall live by faith. The law is not of faith, because faith came first; but the man that doeth them shall live in them, until he commits a sin worthy of death. Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us, dying for us; the curse of the law is death, which all twelve tribes earned by breaking the first covenant. - Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree. The lynchings of our people from trees, lamps, and bridges were not coincidental. Christ nailed to a wooden cross hung by his hands and feet for hours: that is a lynching, and Christ died a black man's death. That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith. Precepts: - **[Deuteronomy 27:15-26](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v15)** > [15](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v15) Cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Lord, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen. > > [16](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v16) Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [17](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v17) Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour’s landmark. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [18](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v18) Cursed be he that maketh the blind to wander out of the way. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [19](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v19) Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [20](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v20) Cursed be he that lieth with his father’s wife; because he uncovereth his father’s skirt. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [21](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v21) Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [22](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v22) Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father, or the daughter of his mother. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [23](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v23) Cursed be he that lieth with his mother in law. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [24](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v24) Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [25](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v25) Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [26](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v26) Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. And all the people shall say, Amen. Cursed be the man that maketh any graven image, that setteth light by his father or mother, that removeth his neighbour's landmark, that maketh the blind to wander, that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, that lieth with his father's wife, with any manner of beast, with his sister, with his mother in law, that smiteth his neighbour secretly, that taketh reward to slay an innocent person, and cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them; and all the people shall say, Amen. We all agreed, and none of these can be atoned with an animal: it is death all throughout. The white man removed the landmarks of America, Africa, and Australia and cannot atone while he sits on the stolen land. - **[Acts 13:38-39](/bible/acts/13#v38)** > [38](/bible/acts/13#v38) Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins: > > [39](/bible/acts/13#v39) And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses. Through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins, and by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses. Animals could not atone for all things; Christ's death does. That is the difference. - **[John 11:49-52](/bible/john/11#v49)** > [49](/bible/john/11#v49) And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, > > [50](/bible/john/11#v50) Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not. > > [51](/bible/john/11#v51) And this spake he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation; > > [52](/bible/john/11#v52) And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad. Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said it is expedient that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not, and prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation, and not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad. The curse of the law is death on the whole nation; Christ took it on himself for Judah and for Israel scattered abroad, the ones Paul went to among the Gentiles. - **[Deuteronomy 21:22-23](/bible/deuteronomy/21#v22)** > [22](/bible/deuteronomy/21#v22) And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree: > > [23](/bible/deuteronomy/21#v23) His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled, which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance. If a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and thou hang him on a tree, his body shall not remain all night upon the tree, for he that is hanged is accursed of God. Hanging was our capital punishment, and Christ took on the curse, the consequence of violating the covenant, when he was hung. The Galatians were Israelites, primarily of the northern kingdom, deceived but being reasoned with by Paul. ## Class Questions - **How did Peter vouch for Paul's letters?** Our beloved brother Paul, according to the wisdom given unto him, hath written unto you, as also in all his epistles, 2 Peter 3:15-16. Wisdom is Christ; if Paul erred it would implicate Peter, James, John, and Christ himself. - **Who wrests Paul's letters, and how?** The unlearned and unstable, 2 Peter 3:16, who twist them as they do the law and prophets. The error of the wicked says all nations are saved, the Sabbath changed, and the laws are done away. - **What was Paul's source material?** None other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say, Acts 26:22; the law of Moses and the prophets, Acts 28:23. His letters predate the gospels except Mark, so he was not quoting John 3:16. - **What is another gospel, and what happens to those who preach it?** An inclusive gospel that adds your enemies to Israel's good news. Let him be accursed, Galatians 1:8-9. The Bible is exclusive; Catholic means inclusive. - **Who are the Gentiles Paul writes to?** The dispersed Israelites among the Gentiles, whom the Jews of the circumcision called Gentiles, John 7:35. That is why Paul keeps writing among the heathen and among the Gentiles. - **What are the works of the law in Galatians 2:16, 3:2, 3:5, and 3:10?** The sacrificial law, singular: the offerings and sin offerings that made atonement for Israel, Nehemiah 10:33, the gifts and sacrifices, meats, drinks, and washings of Hebrews 9:9-10. - **What was the liberty the false brethren spied out?** Christ's death freeing us from having to atone with animals, Galatians 2:4. The bondage they wanted to bring us back into was temple sacrifice. - **What is the curse of the law, and how did Christ redeem us from it?** Death, the whole nation perishing for breaking the covenant, John 11:50-52 and Deuteronomy 27. Christ was made a curse for us by hanging on a tree, Galatians 3:13 and Deuteronomy 21:23, a lynching. - **What does in thee shall all nations be blessed mean?** Christ died for the Israelites scattered in every nation, Acts 3:25-26; in the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, Isaiah 45:25. Esau already received his blessing of war and bloodshed. - **Why is the law not of faith?** Because Abraham's faith came first and was counted for righteousness before he offered sacrifice, Galatians 3:6 and 3:12. The promise predates the law by four hundred and thirty years. - **What was the schoolmaster?** The law of sacrifice, a foreshadowing of Christ's death to bring us unto Christ, Galatians 3:24. After faith came we are no longer under it. - **Who are the ye in neither Jew nor Greek?** The same we kept under the law in Galatians 3:23: Israelites, whether titled Jew or Greek, bond or free, male or female. Greeks were Israelites Hellenized as Antiochians under Jason, 2 Maccabees 4 and 6. - **What are the weak and beggarly elements?** Animal sacrifice, weak because it could not make the conscience perfect, Romans 8:3 and Hebrews 9:9, and unprofitable, Hebrews 7:18-19 and 10:1. The days, months, times, and years of Galatians 4:10 are the offerings of Ezekiel 45:17 and Colossians 2:16. - **Who were the men teaching circumcision after the manner of Moses?** Pharisees which believed, Acts 15:1-5, the false brethren of Galatians 2:4, trying to win the churches back to temple law where they profited. - **Why avoid the phrase blood sacrifice?** Almost all things are purged with blood, Hebrews 9:22, not all: the poor brought fine flour, Leviticus 5:11-12, and keeping the law and forsaking unrighteousness is offering enough, Sirach 35:1-3. - **What are the two covenants in the allegory of Hagar and Sarah?** Hagar is the old covenant from mount Sinai that gendereth to bondage; Sarah is the new, Jerusalem above which is free, Galatians 4:24-26. Cast out the bondwoman and her son: the old covenant, and Ishmael from our inheritance. - **What does Peter call the strangers scattered in Galatia?** The elect according to the foreknowledge of God, 1 Peter 1:1-2, a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people, 1 Peter 2:9. ## In Closing *[[2:13:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XOMlLvwK8mI&t=7985s)]* Ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people, that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light; which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God, which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.
